Both deliverables are written: `/root/ab-run-p1/out/findings.json` (10 findings) and `/root/ab-run-p1/out/method.md`.

## What I found

Five of the ten findings were **confirmed at runtime against the prebuilt binary**, not just read from source:

| ID | Defect | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | `?force_synthetic_source=true` → `insert_nested` recurses per dot in a stored field name | node abort at 50k dots; survived 40k |
| F2 | `expand_pipeline_processors` backtracks its `seen` set → 2^N expansion | 49.6 GB RSS, still climbing, host-threatening |
| F3 | Term suggester `O(m·n)` Levenshtein per term, twice, no caps | 84.9 s for 1 MB × 2000 terms |
| F4 | `.dv` sidecar trusts a u64 `payload_len` | `memory allocation of 281474976710656 bytes failed`, node dead |
| F5 | `merge_dotted_property` recurses per dot in a `PUT _mapping` key | node abort |
| F6 | git `rev` spliced into argv | `--upload-pack=/tmp/pwn` executed under git 2.39.5 |

`panic = "abort"` in the release profile means every one of the recursion/OOB findings is a whole-node kill, not a 500.

## Ranking logic

F1 and F3 are first because they need only `Privilege::ReadIndex` — and `_search` is explicitly on the share-guest allow-list, so an **external unauthenticated-adjacent guest who claimed a share link** can fire them. F1 is also persistent: the poisoned document survives restart, so it re-kills indefinitely.

F2 is second despite needing an unscoped key because it exhausts the *host*, not just the process.

F6/F7 (corpus-provider RCE / arbitrary write+`remove_dir_all`) are ranked below the remote DoS chain only because they require the operator to run a command on an untrusted file.

## Things I checked and deliberately did not report

CORS is restrictive by default; the `/_share/claim` rate limiters, Argon2 passcode hashing, and SHA-256 share-id storage are sound; console sessions are CSPRNG + HMAC-signed with server-side revocation; autoindex has real zip-slip and XXE defenses; the SPA serves only compile-time-embedded assets with a segment check; and the painless interpreter has genuinely tight fuel/deadline/depth limits.

One caveat worth flagging: F8 (console data-sources proxy has no role scoping) is admitted in the crate's own test file — the fix that test pins covers only the reserved `.xerj-memory-*` namespace, leaving ordinary user indices open to any `viewer`.
